correctness.rationale: The theorem concerns the fixed fourteen-vertex Heawood graph. Explicit XOR-model line sets prove the four-point bound and 84 optimum three-flag objects. The compatible-pair completion argument proves precisely three natural types, the unique common-pair triangle covering, and six regular neighbours. A standalone exhaustive direct enumeration of all 1,330 flag triples and all 5,985 four-flag sets, followed by 84 breadth-first searches, verifies the 252 edges, 84 triangles, exact distance counts, eccentricities and exchange lower-bound excess. A second independently coded cyclic incidence model constructs 84 pairs/three completions, verifies all 168 collineations and recomputes three complete orbit distance profiles. Both scripts ran successfully; finite exhaustive computation is valid here because the domain is exactly this finite graph, and no extension to arbitrary projective-plane order is asserted.

value.rationale: The object is the natural graph of all largest induced matchings in the incidence graph of the smallest projective plane, under the minimal feasibility-preserving edge replacement. Unlike a forced increment or table recalculation, the theorem completely determines its three geometric symmetry types, edge-disjoint triangle decomposition, nonuniform eccentricities, all-pairs geodesic counts and exact obstacles to an optimal-length sequence of exchanges. These are structural invariants of the full optimum-configuration space, with practical mathematical use in comparing optimum strong representative systems; the intrinsic question is natural even for a fixed small graph. Significance is limited to this graph, explicitly disclosed.
